result.title: Deformable Contact-Aware 3D Object Placement
result.summary: Current language-guided 3D object placement typically predicts a rigid 6-DoF pose, ignoring the physical reality that indoor placements are dictated by contact. Consequently, predicted poses often float, interpenetrate supports, or fail to deform soft surfaces. We propose Deformable Contact-Aware Placement (DCAP), a framework that reframes placement as a drop-to-equilibrium process. Rather than predicting a static pose, DCAP constructs a semantic release state that specifies the drop location, object scale, and deformable components, allowing a coupled rigid-deformable simulator to settle the object under gravity and friction. This explicitly separates semantic intent from physical realization. Evaluated on a benchmark of 2,063 prompt-asset-scene cases, DCAP significantly outperforms static baselines. On standard placements, it improves VLM Physics & Naturalness by 21.2 points and human preference by 26.5 points over the strongest raw rigid baseline, while reducing mean penetration depth by 72.3%. Compared to simulated rollout baselines, DCAP reduces residual speed by 72.1%. Ultimately, our results prove that physically accurate 3D placement requires modeling semantic intent and physical realization as strictly separate processes.

AI.brief_summary: 针对语言引导的 3D 物体摆放，该文提出 DCAP，把摆放从直接回归刚性 6-DoF 位姿改为「下落至平衡」过程：先由语义意图生成包含落点、尺度与可形变部件的释放状态，再交给刚柔耦合仿真器在重力与摩擦下求解最终位置。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「只预测低维初始状态、由动力学迭代松弛到平衡」的思路，可能与 LVR 中以 latent 初始化加迭代状态更新替代一次性生成相关，但任务域较远，线索需自行核查。
